title: Recording setup
description: The interviewer begins the session in Sandpoint at the Pine Tree and introduces Irene Cook as the shop's owner or co-owner. The opening frames the interview around her personal background and how she came to Sandpoint.

title: Move from California; settling in Sandpoint
description: Cook explains that she and her husband left Santa Cruz because of rising taxes, a fast pace of life, and concerns about raising a family there. After traveling in an Airstream, they bought land near Sandpoint, restored an abandoned house, and settled in Idaho.

title: Family roots in California; husband's injury
description: She describes her upbringing on an apple ranch and says her family still lives in California. She then explains that after the move, money ran out and her husband was badly injured in a truck accident, leaving him disabled.

title: Newcomers; children; education and art
description: The conversation turns to how locals regard newcomers and to Cook's view that Californians are bringing problems north. She also says she has one son, discusses her education, and explains that she learned art mostly outside formal schooling.

title: Adjusting to Sandpoint; arts growth
description: Cook says she misses some city culture but sees Sandpoint developing as more artists and craftspeople move in. She believes this growth exposes local residents to new ideas and broadens the town's life.

title: Natural foods and home economy
description: Cook details a household economy based on making food from scratch, gardening, drying, sprouting, grinding flour, and using raw milk. She presents this routine as economical, healthy, and tied to her stamina for work.

title: Childbirth; health practices
description: She recounts giving birth to Hans shortly after arriving at the hospital and then returning quickly to the store. She connects that experience to yoga, jogging, meditation, and the health turnaround she achieved after leaving California.

title: Family health beliefs
description: Cook says she likes helping others but does not press her views on them. She contrasts her current health practices with her family's habits, attributing some of her earlier ill health partly to sprays and describing her parents and sister as resistant to natural foods.

title: Women's movement; equal rights amendment
description: Asked about women's liberation, Cook says she has mixed feelings: she supports equal pay and wider opportunity for women but distrusts the movement's leadership and worries it may deepen social division and government control.

title: Government control and land-use planning
description: She opposes federal land-use planning and favors local decision-making, arguing that distant regulation erodes property rights. She says local government is preferable because people can respond directly to decisions affecting their own communities.

title: Women's roles and self-reliance
description: The discussion returns to women's changing roles, and Cook argues women should be educated and skilled because hardship can force them to support themselves. She points to women's work as maids or waitresses as evidence of the need for better preparation.

title: Closing remarks
description: The interviewer ends the session because the party must leave Sandpoint, thanks Cook for her time, and expresses interest in continuing the interview on a future visit. Cook says the conversation was a pleasure.
